newsitem.title: USA: Lott says Clinton woes may delay U.S. budget deal.
newsitem.headline: Lott says Clinton woes may delay U.S. budget deal.

text.p: Senate Republican leader Trent Lott said on Sunday that President Clinton's 1996 campaign finance woes may be delaying progress toward a balanced budget agreeement.
Lott, on the NBC television program "Meet the Press," said he was disappointed and basically tired of waiting for serious negotiations to begin on a package to balance the budget by the year 2002.
"If we don't see some quick action here, in the next week or ten days, the president, I think, is beginning to get in the position of marginalizing himself," the Mississippi lawmaker said.
In reply to a question, Lott said the almost daily stream of allegations of improper Democratic fund raising on behalf of Clinton's reelection must be a "distraction" for Clinton.

"I assume, maybe, that has something to do with it," he said, of the delay in getting negotiations going. Congress is supposed to pass a resolution setting budget priorities by April 15, but Lott blamed what he described as Clinton's inaction for making that unlikely to happen.
He referred to an unspecified "indication" that Clinton would meet congressional leaders and budget committee chiefs this week to talk about narrowing partisan budget differences.
"I understand now that that may slip a week," Lott said, without elaborating. The White House did not immediately return a phone call seeking comment.
Lott said he understood that little or nothing had come from low-level talks over the past two weeks between administration officials and congressional budget experts.
"The reports I'm getting is that basically they've been talking about how nice it is they're talking," he said.
Clinton indicated last week he was still optimistic that a deal might be struck with the Republican-controlled Congress.
"I really believe we'll get a bipartisan balanced budget agreement this year. I think it is the right thing to do for the country," he said.

White House Press Secretary Mike McCurry added: "I think that we always made clear that we want to work real hard to balance the budget, and it would most likely be necessary for the president to talk to the bipartisan leadership at length, if we're going to do so. And he's prepared to do that."
